data.narrative:
TAE Technologies is a Series G nuclear energy company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The valuation universe comprises ten comparable companies: three public equities (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and seven private firms including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy. The private peer set reflects the fragmented and nascent state of advanced nuclear financing.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised ($1.3B) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.25x multiplier typical of Series G to next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $1.6B. A peer-median approach was not feasible: while six same-sector comparables exist, insufficient datapoints emerged within narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-valuation-tier cohorts), and an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $1.9B, centered at $1.6B. Material uncertainties include the absence of robust comparable transaction data at this stage in the nuclear sector, the nascent profitability profile of peer companies, and forward-looking regulatory and commercialization timelines. The single-method result should be stress-tested against management guidance on capital needs and product deployment milestones before final valuation commitment.
